title: Serially homologous parts derive from many repeated similar elements in progenitors

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Serially homologous parts derive from many repeated similar elements in progenitors

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Serial homologies within one individual (skull and vertebrae, jaws and legs of crustaceans, floral parts and leaves) arise because the progenitors of vertebrates, articulates and flowering plants had many repeated similar parts, which natural selection adapted to diverse purposes while inheritance retained a fundamental resemblance.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: An indefinite repetition of the same part or organ is the common characteristic (as Owen has observed) of all low or little-modified forms; therefore we may readily believe that the unknown progenitor of the vertebrata possessed many vertebræ; the unknown progenitor of the articulata, many segments; and the unknown progenitor of flowering plants, many spiral whorls of leaves.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIII, “Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs”; section “MORPHOLOGY, between members of the same class, between parts of the same individual”. Scope: vertebrates, articulates (arthropods and annelids) and flowering plants

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch13-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.59

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modularity and ancestral repetition can be tested in particular systems. Deep-time coverage and cross-lineage harmonization are insufficient to resolve the complete mechanism.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map serial-element counts, developmental gene expression and morphology onto vertebrate, arthropod and flowering-plant phylogenies to infer whether their ancestors had repeated similar modules subsequently differentiated. Reconstructed high repetition at the relevant ancestors supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Comparable developmental data are sparse across all three lineages.

Deep ancestral states are highly model-dependent.

The historical term articulata combines lineages no longer treated as one group.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.62
analysis feasibility: 0.48
data existence: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Counts of repeated parts and their distribution on a tree are measurable, but the progenitor story needs a fossil or ancestral reconstruction that is only partly available. Existing fossil occurrences and matrices can test a subset of vertebrates and arthropods and are weak for the floral-leaf comparison. Circular definitions of 'low' and the co-option alternative keep discriminating power modest.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test two linked predictions: earlier or less modified members of vertebrates, arthropods and flowering plants show more numerous repeated parts, and ancestral-state or fossil reconstructions give those progenitors many similar segments, vertebrae or leaf-like organs. The claim is confirmed if repetition declines along derived branches and stem fossils are highly repetitive, and refuted if repetition is unrelated to phylogenetic grade or stem fossils already show specialized, non-repeated organs.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Low or little-modified' has often been defined by the presence of many repeated parts, which builds the predicted pattern into the ranking.

The relevant early fossils are incomplete, especially for soft segmentation and for the origin of floral organs.

A shared patterning pathway can be co-opted later, producing serial organs without an ancestor that already possessed many of them.

fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.45
data existence: 0.6
discriminating power: 0.4
